MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  August 28, 2018

A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the
Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor
Sachs at 5:00 p.m., on August 28, 2018, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted
by 5:00 p.m. on August 23, 2018, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also
posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman
P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Bucknum (arrived at 5:02 p.m.)
  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Mayor Pro Tem Raths
  Mayor Sachs

City Council Minutes  1  August 28, 2018
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

Mayor Sachs recessed the meeting to Closed Session at the hour of 5:01 p.m. The City Council
reconvened at 6:03 p.m. with all five City Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Bill Curley announced that the City Council addressed two matters in Closed
Session dealing with litigation. The Council provided direction to staff but no reportable action
occurred.

INVOCATION: Council Member Kelley

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Mayor Sachs

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Bob Hayes, M.V.: in tribute to John McCain, he read the late Senator's final letter to the public.

M.J. Nejad, M.V.: introduced himself and his business, MJ's Pet Spaw & Boutique, which provides
a variety of services including mobile grooming and doggy daycare from its new location in
Olympiad Plaza. The website address is www.mjspetspaw.com.

Bill Moorhead, M.V.: announced that he is a principal engineer for the City of Anaheim and has
been in the water business for 42 years. He is also a candidate for the Moulton Niguel Water
District Board of Directors and he commended the City Council for its political sign policy.

Mahmoud El-Farra, M.V.: stated that he is a candidate for Mission Viejo City Council and he
discussed San Diego Gas and Electric’s significant rate increases. He said that the City can lower
utility rates by moving to Community Choice Energy (CCE) which will create a competitive
electricity marketplace. Mr. El-Farra urged the City Council to begin a feasibility report to see how
much can be saved.

Barbara Schulman, M.V.: announced that she is running for Saddleback School Board and is the
only Mission Viejo resident running. She believes in attracting and retaining teachers, safety in
schools and communication with families. Ms. Schulman stated that communities succeed when
students succeed.

Juan Gonzalez, M.V.: introduced himself as the recently assigned Local Public Affairs Manager
for Southern California Gas. He mentioned the Dig Alert program and reminded residents to call
811 before doing any kind of yard work that involves digging. Mr. Gonzalez said he looks forward
to working with the City.

31.  Library Automated System Software and Hardware Support Agreement

  Mayor Sachs asked how many more years staff is expecting to have these annual payments
  and are they aggregated upwards of 3%. He further asked about the expected life of the
  Library Automated system.

  Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander responded that this is year six with
  the existing system and it is up to the City's discretion as to when to exit the agreement and
  purchase a new system. She noted that purchase of a new system would require payment
  of approximately the same amount ($70,000) annually and staff plans to budget for a new
  system in the next budget cycle.

  Motion made by Mayor Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve
  issuance of a purchase order for 1-year in the amount of $69,940.71 for maintenance and
  support of the Library Automated Systems (ALS) Software and Hardware Agreement with
  SirsiDynix, Inc.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

32.  Tyler Munis ERP Financial, HR, and Payroll Software Renewal

  Mayor Sachs asked how long staff is expecting to make these annual payments and what
  is the expected life of the Financial, HR and Payroll software.

  Jackie Alexander, Director of Information Technology, responded that the City has a five-
  year negotiated agreement with the vendor and has capped the renewal rate at 5%. She
  stated that this particular renewal came in at about 3%. Like the Library system previously
  discussed, the City can decide when to exit but since this is a newer system, she said staff
  does not plan to replace it within the next two years. Director Alexander stated that she
  doesn't have a lifetime estimate but at the time of purchase, staff anticipated $200,000 for
  the five years but she will double-check that figure and notify the City Council by email.

  Motion made by Mayor Sachs, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve purchase
  order to Tyler Technologies, Inc. for 1-year renewal of software licensing and support for
  Munis ERP Financial, Human Resources, and Payroll system in the amount of $65,027.00.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

City Council Minutes  8  August 28, 2018
   AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Raths, and Sachs
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

33.  Lease of Hardware for Data Storage, Backup and Recovery

  Mayor Sachs asked if this is a purchase or a lease.

  Director of Information Technology Jackie Alexander responded that it is a lease but staff
  sometimes uses the term purchase because the City will buy the equipment for $1 at the
  end of the term of the lease. She noted that the City typically keeps this type of equipment
  for five years.

  Council Member Bucknum asked about out-of-state backup due to the potential for natural
  disasters in California. Director Alexander responded that the City uses the San Diego
  location for backup and does not currently have an out-of-state site. She noted that the San
  Diego location is on a different fault line and electric grid than Mission Viejo City Hall is
  and staff is beginning to explore cloud storage. Ms. Alexander said that out-of-state backup
  services are more expensive than the San Diego location and staff feels it is a preferred
  method.

  Council Member Bucknum asked that the City consider looking into out-of-state backup
  and bring the item to a future agenda.

  Motion made by Mayor Sachs, seconded by Council Member Bucknum, to approve
  entering into agreement for a 3-year lease with Dell Financial Services for purchase of Data
  Domain hardware and issuance of purchase orders to Dell Financial Services annually for
  $41,282.26 for a total of $123,846.78.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

STAFF REPORTS

City Attorney’s Report

City Attorney Bill Curley discussed the conclusion of the California Voting Rights Act (CVRA)
matter and announced he will bring an agenda item to disband the CVRA ad hoc committee at the
next meeting and will ask the Council to consider forming a new Voter Education Ad Hoc
Committee.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS (Continued)

Council Member Bucknum

Council Member Bucknum outlined her attendance at summer events including a luau party at
Montanoso Recreation Center, the grand re-opening of the Felipe Tennis and Recreation Center
which offers a variety of new opportunities for residents, the ribbon cutting ceremony for a “Little
Free Library” on Sadaba street in Mission Viejo, the City’s campout at Cordova Park, National
Night Out, and the Cardboard Boat Derby. Council Member Bucknum thanked Annie Nelson with
American Soldier Network who helped her organize a collection of t-shirts and socks for
firefighters battling the Holy Fire. She said the lion’s share of the donations came from Stephanie
Vangaurd who is a member of the Mission Viejo Elks Club and owner of Bongo Ink in Lake
Forest. Council Member Bucknum discussed upcoming events including a Patriot Day Ceremony
before the next City Council meeting in honor of 9/11 and on September 15, the Innercoastal
Watershed Cleanup and a document shredding drive through event at Mission Viejo High School.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell said that he enjoyed the Chamber of Commerce Restaurant Week and
he also attended the Chamber mixer last week at the Shops at Mission Viejo. He reported that the
City Council Minutes  11  August 28, 2018
 Economic Development ad hoc committee met a few times over the summer and they had some
very productive discussions about moving forward with plans to enhance business development,
especially for the shopping center across the street from city hall. Council Member Goodell
discussed the Olympic Promotion Committee and stated that there is a lot happening with new
innovations and the changes at the Marguerite Aquatics Complex. He said the committee is
growing and the members have great ideas and energy.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley announced that she attended most of the summer events that Council
Member Bucknum outlined and she thanked Library Director Genesis Hansen and Senior
Librarian Allison Tran for putting on a fantastic summer reading program. She said that four of
her grandchildren participated and the incentives and prizes were so great. She commended
Library staff for doing a fantastic job with the programs that they offer for all ages. Council
Member Kelley noted that there has been a huge outcry from residents about San Diego Gas &
Electric’s rates. She said she has been in contact with SDG&E representative Duane Cave to seek
information. She also attended a meeting last Friday with the City Manager and representatives
from Assemblyman Brough and Senator Bates offices. She shared some of the answers that were
given at the meeting as to why the rates are so high and she encouraged SDG&E customers to
write to the California Public Utilities Commission and/or file a complaint. Letters can be sent to
the Public Advisor’s office at publicadvisor@cpuc.ca.gov. In closing, Council Member Kelley
announced that the Community of Character word for the month of August is self-control.

Mayor Pro Tem Raths

Mayor Pro Tem Raths noted that his electric bill has been stable because of his solar panels and
given the current situation with electricity rates, he said he feels bad for those who don't have solar.
He announced that he was honored to represent the City of Mission Viejo at the Orange County
Fair on August 8 for a flag raising ceremony and he commented on the Chamber’s great Restaurant
Week event. Mayor Pro Tem Raths said he is a big fan of the Chamber and its membership is
growing all the time. In conclusion, he thanked Orange County Fire Authority and Orange County
Sheriff’s Department personnel for all they do to keep Mission Viejo residents safe.

Mayor Sachs

Mayor Sachs congratulated Boy Scout Richard Kramer who was in attendance for the entire
meeting tonight and he asked resident Barbara Schulman to stay after the meeting so he can share
some information with her. He noted that one big event that his colleagues forgot to mention was
the ice cream social with the City’s firefighters and Sheriff’s deputies. The first-time event was a
great success with more than 200 kids enjoying themselves and the ice cream. Mayor Sachs
announced that he attended 23 meetings over the summer break and 10 days with his wife in remote
areas that had no cell service, which he recommended for everyone. Regarding the SDG&E billing
situation, Mayor Sachs he said he doesn’t know who is subsidizing who because those with solar
sell their abundance of electricity to the utility companies for a low amount and the electric
companies sell it back for a large profit. He said joining Community Choice Energy (CCE) sounds
good on the outside, but the City would pay the utility companies a very large departure fee and
would have to pay to rent the infrastructure so it is not as simple as it may sound.
City Council Minutes  12  August 28, 2018
